newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition party rejects pact with another.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition party rejects pact with another.

text.p: Mexico's conservative opposition National Action Party (PAN) rejected on Friday a proposal to join forces with the leftist opposition Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) in July's congressional elections.

Following an 11-hour meeting of top party leaders, PAN President Felipe Calderon announced that his party would reject the PRD's offer to team up against the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Pary (PRI).

"The PAN will launch its own candidates with our own platform, that is to say not in convergence or in coalition as the law allows," Calderon said in an interview with the television news programme 24 Hours.

The decision is likely to cause relief in the beleaguered ruling party. Its leaders have alternately criticised the proposed alliance as either anti-democratic or a sign that opposition parties lacked confidence to run on their own.
The PRD, which is not nearly as strong as the PAN, proposed the alliance as a means to achieve their common goal of upsetting the PRI.
But the two parties are poles apart ideologically on most issues, with the PAN a fervent backer of free enterprise while the PRD supports government supports and guarantees for the poor.
Pollsters and political analysts have been saying in the run-up to the July elections that the PRI stands to lose its majority in Congress for the first time in 67 years in power.
The PRI, which historically has maintained itself in power, has seen its popularity plummet because of a severe economic recession and a series of political and corruption scandals in recent years.

Nonetheless, President Ernesto Zedillo has pledged clean elections and made the rule of law a central plank of his administration. When he was easily elected to office in 1994, international observers declared the voting free of fraud.
